decisions: Use the inherited Core complexity model only as conceptual reference; do not create ProjectReference, binary reference, local package dependency, or transitive dependency on inherited projects.
Keep the Phase 2 model inside ComplexityAnalysis.Analyzers, preferably under analyzer/src/ComplexityAnalysis.Analyzers/Model/.
Use a lightweight immutable model centered on polynomial-logarithmic, exponential, factorial, composite, constant, and unknown complexity forms.
Normalize multiplicative constants away for initial Big-O modeling.
Represent input variables as Roslyn-free immutable value objects and do not infer ordering between independent variables.
Use explicit growth comparison results: Less, Equivalent, Greater, and Incomparable.
Define composition operations as Sequential, Nested, and Branching with conservative simplification only when mathematically safe.
Step 2 implemented only atomic expressions; composition, growth comparison, and Roslyn extraction remain unimplemented.
Model types are internal analyzer infrastructure; tests access them through InternalsVisibleTo without making a public NuGet API.
O(1) and Unknown are distinct canonical immutable values; Unknown is never treated as constant.
Polynomial(variable, 0) normalizes to O(1), while direct polynomial-log construction rejects the duplicate k=0 and j=0 representation.
Complexity variable names are accepted when they start with an ASCII letter and then contain only ASCII letters or digits.
ComplexityGrowthComparer models ordering by expression family and same-variable mathematical rules instead of using a single arbitrary score.
Constant complexity compares below known non-constant expressions regardless of variable name because it has no input variable.
Unknown comparisons are Incomparable except Unknown compared with Unknown, which is Equivalent.
Composition uses ComplexityOperation.Sequential, ComplexityOperation.Nested, and ComplexityOperation.Maximum; ComplexityComposer.Branching maps branching semantics to the Maximum operation.
Sequential and Branching use ComplexityGrowthComparer to keep the dominant term only when comparison is safe; independent variables are preserved as CompositeComplexity.
Nested eliminates O(1) factors and multiplies same-variable polynomial-log terms by adding polynomial and log exponents.
Composition involving Unknown returns Unknown to avoid hiding inconclusive analysis.
constraints: Do not implement Roslyn extraction, SyntaxNode analysis, SemanticModel analysis, ControlFlowGraph analysis, loop analysis, LINQ/BCL mappings, interprocedural analysis, call graphs, recurrence solving, CodeFixProvider, Workspaces, MathNet, SymPy, memory, amortized, probabilistic, parallel, or confidence-scoring features in Phase 2.
Do not modify inherited projects outside analyzer/.
Do not create a second NuGet package.
The model itself must not depend on Roslyn APIs.
BIG9000 and all Phase 1 behavior must continue to work.
